entities.summary:
The Russian Revolution of 1905 was a pivotal event in world history, shaping the course of modern Russia and influencing the global trajectory of revolutionary movements. It was a period of mass political and social unrest that spread through vast areas of the Russian Empire, from January 22, 1905, to June 16, 1907. Key figures involved included Tsar Nicholas II, Leon Trotsky, and Vladimir Lenin, among others.

The revolution began with a wave of strikes and protests, sparked by the Russo-Japanese War and the government's refusal to grant civil liberties. The movement gained momentum with the Bloody Sunday Massacre, where Tsar Nicholas II ordered his troops to fire on a peaceful crowd of protesters in St. Petersburg. The revolution eventually led to the establishment of the Duma, Russia's first parliament, and the eventual rise of the Bolsheviks.

The Russian Revolution of 1905 had a lasting impact on world history. It paved the way for the 1917 Russian Revolution, which led to the establishment of the Soviet Union, and influenced similar revolutionary movements around the world. The event also led to significant changes in Russia's politics, economy, and society, shaping the country's trajectory for generations to come.

The revolution's legacy can be seen in the words of Leon Trotsky, who wrote, 'The Russian Revolution of 1905 was the first great upsurge of the Russian people against the absolutism of the Romanov dynasty.' This event marked a turning point in world history, shaping the course of modern Russia and influencing the global trajectory of revolutionary movements.
